subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Ignoring New Product Launches
description: A fast breakdown of Ignoring New Product Launches for builders.

hook.text: A new product launches with zero historical data. The forecast model says zero demand. The shelf is empty on day one.

buildup.text: Statistical models rely on history. New products have none, creating a blind spot in the forecast.

discovery.text: Analog modeling—using similar past launches as proxies—gives new products a demand shape to start from.

twist.text: Marketing hype often inflates launch forecasts. Reality rarely matches the PowerPoint projections.

climax.text: A structured new product introduction (NPI) process with cross-functional input reduces launch forecast errors.

punchline.text: No history doesn't mean no forecast. Use analogs.

quiz.question: How can new products be forecasted without history?
options: Using analog products with similar profiles
